sum: A road-access teahouse trek along the ridges of lower Solu to the 4,065 m summit of Pikey Peak, then down to the Sherpa village of Junbesi and out from Phaplu.

guide.note: Pikey lies outside the national parks and conservation areas, and nobody checks for a guide on this ridge. On paper the TIMS card for the route is tied to the Nepal Tourism Board rule of April 2023 that foreign trekkers walk with a licensed guide; in practice many people go independently. A guide earns the fee where the footpath keeps leaving and rejoining the jeep track above Jhapre, in the fog that settles on the ridge most afternoons, and by phoning ahead to lodges that open only when someone is expected.

access: Dhap lies on the road from Okhaldhunga to Salleri, a full day's drive from Kathmandu. Shared jeeps bound for Salleri leave the capital before dawn and will drop you there. The trek ends at Phaplu, where jeeps leave for Kathmandu early each morning and a flight operates on some days.

photo.a: Heaps of colourful prayer flags cover the rocky summit of Pikey Peak, with a line of snow-covered Himalayan peaks on the horizon under a deep blue sky.
photo.c: Prayer flags on the summit of Pikey Peak

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
trekking card and local entry fees where charged
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
jeep or bus from Kathmandu and back

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: A seat in a shared jeep between Kathmandu and the Solu roadhead, each way
tips: Carry cash for the whole trek. The only cash machines are in Salleri, close to the end.
Take a filter or purification tablets and carry two litres on the ridge days. In the dry months there are few springs between Jhapre and the base camp.
Lodges at the base camp are small. In October, November and April have someone phone ahead from Jhapre.
Pikey is outside the national park, so there is no park fee. The TIMS card is the only paperwork and nothing on the route checks it; an agency arranges it if you go with a guide.
Bring a headlamp and a proper down jacket for the summit morning, even if the days feel warm.

days.note: Leave before dawn. The road follows the BP Highway to Khurkot and the Sun Koshi to Ghurmi, then climbs through Okhaldhunga to the ridge at Dhap. You step out about 1,450 m higher than you started, so keep the evening quiet.
why: A jump from 1,400 m to sleep at 2,850 m in a single day.

days.note: The route keeps to the ridge north of Dhap through the hamlet of Sigane, mostly on the jeep track with footpath short-cuts across its bends. Farmland and pine give way to forest, and Everest and Numbur are on the skyline by the time you reach Jhapre.

Follow the track to Bhulbhule, then leave it for a forest trail along the ridge, past mani walls and out onto yak pasture that leads round the hillside to the lodges. You gain 800 m of sleeping height, so expect a mild headache and drink plenty.

days.t: Pikey Peak at sunrise, then down to Junbesi
days.note: Start by headlamp for the 425 m climb to the summit, about ninety minutes, and be there for sunrise. Afterwards follow the trail round to the saddle at Jase Bhanjyang and descend through forest to meet the old Jiri trail above Junbesi. A long day, nearly all of it downhill.

A rest day with a purpose. Walk an hour and a half up the valley to Thupten Chholing, a large monastery with several hundred monks and nuns, and come back for lunch. Junbesi's own monastery and lanes fill the afternoon.
Down the Junbesi Khola through farms and pine forest, partly on the jeep road, to the airstrip town of Phaplu. Book tomorrow's jeep seat as soon as you arrive; they leave very early.
Jeeps leave around five in the morning and reach Kathmandu by late afternoon, traffic and road works allowing. If a flight is operating and the sky is clear, the journey takes half an hour instead.
